notes: Each live message is archived, ingested, indexed and notified individually; there is no receive/publish time window.
AOT pipeline: each target sampled for 20 seconds, includes bounded live history archive writes, excludes Flutter rendering.
UI: fullyLive policy, independent samples after warmup; scrolling, search, send, overlapping/unordered history pages and return-to-latest are exercised.
Frame duration is max(buildDuration, rasterDuration); slow frame threshold is 16.67ms.
History request delays simulate server latency; they do not merge or throttle the live message stream.
History and live cache are in-memory; all runtime data resets on restart.
Results are machine-specific; iOS and Android physical devices have not been benchmarked.
UI results were rerun with 20 retained chat sessions; AOT results are retained from the preceding history pagination revision and were not rerun.
Session cache retains the 20 most recently opened windows; draft storage survives provider disposal and window eviction.
UI uses Riverpod 3.5.0 native Notifier families. Stores contain no listener callbacks; live notifier handles are registered by build/onDispose and only changed states are published synchronously.

49 tests pass, including synchronous per-message notifications, actual widget rebuild scope, direct publication isolation, duplicate-ID rejection, provider invalidation/disposal and bounded session/history behavior.

Final UI sample: 1000/s frame P95 1.548ms; 5000/s frame P95 4.007ms. The earlier retained-session revision measured 1.642ms and 1.398ms respectively; high-rate frame cost has increased. These separate local runs do not establish the sole cause of the difference.
